==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:often}}
From {{inh|en|enm|often}}, alteration (with final ''-n'' added due to analogy with {{cog|enm|selden|t=seldom}}) of {{inh|en|enm|ofte}}, {{m|enm|oft}}, from {{inh|en|ang|oft|t=often}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ufta}}, {{m|gem-pro|*uftō||often}}. 
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|affen}}, {{m|sco|aften}}, {{m|sco|af'en}}, {{m|sco|oaffen}}, {{m|sco|oaften}}, {{m|sco|oftin|t=often}}, {{cog|frr|aaft}}, {{m|frr|oftem}}, {{m|frr|oofting|t=often}}, {{cog|stq|oafte|t=often}}, {{cog|de|-}}, {{cog|lb|-}} and {{cog|pdc|oft|t=often}}, {{cog|yi|אָפֿט|t=often}}, {{cog|da|-}}, {{cog|nb|-}} and {{cog|nn|ofte|t=often}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|sv|ofta|t=often}}, {{cog|is|oft|t=often}}, {{cog|got|𐌿𐍆𐍄𐌰|t=often}}.
{{col-bottom}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɒfən/|/ˈɒftən/|/ˈɔː-/<q:East Anglia, Traditional RP>|a=RP,AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɔfən/|/ˈɔftən/|a=SSB,Scotland}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɒfən/|/ˈɒftən/|[ˈɔ̟fən]|[ˈɔ̟ftən]|a=NZ}}
* {{a|en|US|CA}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɔfən/|/ˈɔftən/|a=non-cot-caught}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɑfən/|/ˈɑftən/|/ˈɒ-/|a=cot-caught}}
*** {{audio|en|En-us-often.ogg|a=US,cot-caught}}
* Historically, the {{ic|/t/}} was pronounced but the current pronunciation was standardized after it stopped being pronounced (as in, e.g., {{m|en|listen}}, {{m|en|soften}}, {{m|en|glisten}}). Therefore, the modern forms where the {{ic|/t/}} is pronounced are spelling pronunciations. The traditional {{ic|/t/}}-less form is considered by many to be more correct for that reason.{{cln|en|spelling pronunciations}}
* {{hmp|en|orphan|aa=non-rhotic,lot-cloth split}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒfən|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|oft|en}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|more,er}}

# [[frequently|Frequently]]; [[many]] [[times]] on different occasions.
#: {{synonyms|en|a lot|q2=archaic except US|oftentimes|typically|Thesaurus:often}}
#: {{antonyms|en|infrequently|occasionally|rarely|seldom|q5=literary except India|unoften|Thesaurus:rarely}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''often''' walk to work when the weather is nice.}}
#: {{ux|en|I’ve been going to the movies more '''often''' since a new theatre opened near me.}}
#: {{ux|en|It can't be said too '''often''' / '''often''' enough.}}
#* {{RQ:Critical Pronouncing Dictionary|page=578|ppage=1|passage=☞ This word [{{m|en|wrap}}] is '''often''' pronounced ''wrop'', rhyming with ''top'', even by ſpeakers much above the vulgar.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=55
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/business/21579011-president-proposes-new-round-intellectual-property-reform-obama-goes-troll-hunting Obama goes troll-hunting]|passage=According to this saga of intellectual-property misanthropy, these creatures [patent trolls] roam the business world, buying up patents and then using them to demand extravagant payouts from companies they accuse of infringing them. '''Often''', their victims pay up rather than face the costs of a legal battle.}}
